lines.japanese:
とある一日。
　朔屋が遅い昼食を摂っていた時の事。
lines.english:
One day.
Sakuya was eating a late lunch.

lines.japanese: 双子たちが、ちょっと仕事がある、なに簡単な仕事だよ、と持ちかけてきたのだが。
lines.english: The twins approached him with a little job. Nothing difficult, they said. A simple job.

lines.japanese:
仕事というのは、この港の倉庫に行って、そこにいる人物と会って、これこれの書類を渡してくること。なるほど聞く限りでは、簡単である。
　簡単そうではある、あるけれどしかし───
lines.english:
He was to go to a warehouse in this port, meet someone there, and hand over some documents. Simple enough, from the sound of it.
It sounded simple. Certainly. But—

lines.japanese:
日頃から、脱走の機会を窺っているとばれている朔屋を、なんでその絶好の糸口である陸へ遣わそうというのか。
　朔屋にしては珍しい勘働きで厄介事の兆し感じ取り、慎重になったという。
lines.english:
They knew he was always looking for a chance to desert. Why send him ashore, offering the perfect opening?
With intuition rare for him, Sakuya sensed trouble and grew cautious.

lines.japanese:
「ええー……？
　水夫君達の誰か、遣いに出せば済む事なんじゃ？」
lines.english: “Uhh… Couldn't you just send one of the sailors?”

lines.japanese: 面倒事は朔屋の最も遠ざけたいところ。それもあってと否むも、
lines.english: Trouble was what he most wished to keep away from. For that reason, too, he refused. But—

lines.japanese:
「なかなかそうもいかないのよねこれが。
　あの子達は根っからの船員暮らしで、
　船からそんなに離れたがらないの」
lines.english: “It's not that easy, actually. They've lived as sailors all their lives. They don't like getting far from the ship.”

lines.japanese: と、なおも朔屋を口説こうとする。渋る朔屋に、双子たちは色仕掛けとしなだれかかった。
lines.english: They continued trying to persuade him. When he resisted, they leaned against him and resorted to seduction.

lines.japanese: 「だいたい朔屋さあ、こないだのアクちゃんの件では、あんたのせいでひどい目に遭ったわけ」
lines.english: “Besides, Sakuya, we had an awful time with little Aku the other day because of you.”

lines.japanese: 「なんであれが俺のせい？」
lines.english: “How was that my fault?”

lines.japanese: 「だって考えてみれば、あの日あんたが盗み呑みの罰で引っぱっていかれずにさ、始めからアクちゃん採りに行ってきてくれたなら」
lines.english: “Think about it. If you hadn't been dragged away for stealing rum, and had just gone to get little Aku for us in the first place—”

lines.japanese: 「あたし独りで行こうなんて気も起こさなかったわけ。だからあんたのせい」
lines.english: “I wouldn't have thought of going alone. So it's your fault.”

lines.japanese: 「おおなんたる責任転嫁」
lines.english: “What a magnificent way to shift the blame.”

lines.japanese:
「まあまあ、そう拗[す]ねないで。
　今回、お遣いちゃんとしてこられたらぁ」
lines.english: “Come on, don't sulk. If you do this errand properly…”

lines.japanese:
「ね、船室のさ、普段人が来ないとこ、
　一つとっておくから───」
lines.english: “We'll reserve a cabin. Somewhere people don't usually come—”

lines.japanese: 「で、あとは……二人っきり……ね？」
lines.english: “And then… just the two of us… right?”

lines.japanese: 朔屋の両腕をそれぞれ取って胸の中にかき抱き、唇耳朶に寄せて囁きの、余りに判りやすすぎる飴と鞭だが、下半身直結男の朔屋君には抗[あらが]いがたい誘惑だし、久しぶりに陸に上がっての仕事であるのは確かだ。逃げ出す機会だって見えてくるのではないか？　そのあたりの諸々鑑みて結局朔屋は、お遣いを引き受ける事にする。
lines.japaneseRuby: 朔屋の両腕をそれぞれ取って胸の中にかき抱き、唇[R耳朶^じだ]に寄せて囁きの、余りに判りやすすぎる飴と鞭だが、下半身直結男の朔屋君には抗[あらが]いがたい誘惑だし、久しぶりに陸に上がっての仕事であるのは確かだ。逃げ出す機会だって見えてくるのではないか？　そのあたりの諸々鑑みて結局朔屋は、お遣いを引き受ける事にする。
lines.english: Each took an arm and clasped it to her breasts, bringing her lips to his ear to whisper. An excessively obvious carrot and stick. Yet to Sakuya, a man wired directly to his lower half, the temptation was irresistible. And it was certainly a job ashore, for the first time in a while. Perhaps an opportunity to escape would present itself. Considering all these things, he ultimately accepted the errand.

lines.japanese: 囲いの葦簀から濛とたなびいた湯気は、青年の胸元にかかって湿り、熱く、すぐに颯と流れて後は涼しい。はたまた龍の吐息か火の山の息吹か、なんの、もっと俗で、湯気は大蒜、韮だの五辛の香味たっぷり孕んで鼻に利いたし、ぎとつく屋台の竹籠に並んだのは、ふっくらとして、白く柔らかで、うねってちょんと角が立った皮の造作も胃の腑に雄弁に囁きかける、豚饅、中華饅頭の出来たてのところで。うっかり湯気と匂いの流れに踏みこもうものなら、いつ銭を払ったのかも判然としないままに経木剥がして噛みついて、熱い汁が舌を焼いたところで我に返るところ間違いなし、実に深層心理辺りに巧みに作用する湯気であることは屋台の店主自身よくよく心得て、承知で盛大に蒸籠を蒸かしていたわけだが。
lines.japaneseRuby: 囲いの[R葦簀^よしず]から[R濛^もう]とたなびいた湯気は、青年の胸元にかかって湿り、熱く、すぐに[R颯^さつ]と流れて後は涼しい。はたまた龍の吐息か火の山の息吹か、なんの、もっと俗で、湯気は[R大蒜^ニンニク]、[R韮^ニラ]だの五辛の香味たっぷり孕んで鼻に利いたし、ぎとつく屋台の竹籠に並んだのは、ふっくらとして、白く柔らかで、うねってちょんと角が立った皮の造作も胃の腑に雄弁に囁きかける、豚饅、中華饅頭の出来たてのところで。うっかり湯気と匂いの流れに踏みこもうものなら、いつ銭を払ったのかも判然としないままに[R経木^きょうぼく]剥がして噛みついて、熱い汁が舌を焼いたところで我に返るところ間違いなし、実に深層心理辺りに巧みに作用する湯気であることは屋台の店主自身よくよく心得て、承知で盛大に蒸籠を蒸かしていたわけだが。
lines.english: Steam billowed from behind a reed screen and drifted against the young man's chest: damp, hot, then swiftly gone, leaving coolness. A dragon's exhalation? The breath of a volcano? Nothing so exalted. The steam carried the rich scents of the five pungent herbs—garlic, chives, and the like—straight to his nose. On the greasy stall, arranged in bamboo baskets, lay freshly steamed pork buns. Plump, soft, and white, their wrappers twisted to little points that spoke eloquently to the stomach. Step carelessly into that drifting steam and fragrance, and without even knowing when you had paid, you would be peeling away the thin wooden wrapper and biting. Only when hot juice burned your tongue would you come to yourself. Steam that worked skillfully upon the deeper mind. The stallholder knew this perfectly well and deliberately kept the baskets steaming lavishly. But—

lines.japanese:
「……なああんた、買わないんならさぁ、
　さっさとよそ行ってくれんかね？
　客でもねえのが突っ立ってられると、
　邪魔でしょうがねえんだが」
lines.english: “…Listen, if you're not buying, could you go somewhere else? Having someone who isn't a customer standing there is a damned nuisance.”

lines.japanese: 先刻より街角の、二人も立ってしまえば一杯の露店の前を塞がれては、店主ならずとも苦りきるのが当然だ。
lines.english: Sakuya had been blocking the street-corner stall for some time. Two people standing before it would fill its entire frontage. Anyone, not just the owner, would have been thoroughly annoyed.

lines.japanese:
「いいじゃあないかちょっとくらい。
　さっきから見てると客なんか来ないみたいだし」
lines.english: “A little while won't hurt. I've been watching, and you don't seem to have any customers.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ？　なんか言ったか」
lines.english: “What? You say something?”

lines.japanese:
本人は街に擦れたいっぱしの露店商面で凄んだつもりでも、顔が海苔の佃煮の小瓶のラベルのポンチ絵とそっくりときては、渋面は威しの用には立たず、むしろ滑稽味さえ催させる次第で。
　とこうせっかく人格劇の役者としても充分通用しそうな、店主の声回しと顔芸なのに、朔屋ときたら馬耳東風介上の空、蒸籠からむらむら立ち籠める湯気に封筒を翳[かざ]すのに夢中で、亭主などろくに見ていやしない。
lines.english:
The owner meant to intimidate him with the face of an experienced, streetwise vendor. But when that face resembled the cartoon on a little jar of seaweed relish, a scowl could hardly threaten anyone. It was almost funny.
His delivery and facial antics would have done a character actor proud. Sakuya, however, was utterly inattentive. He was engrossed in holding an envelope over the billowing steam, scarcely looking at the man at all.

lines.japanese: 言いつけられた仕事を大人しくこなすだけに留めればいいものを、朔屋は預けられた封書の中味に出歯亀根性抑えがたく、糊付けにされた封筒を開けてみようとしているのである。鋏を入れたり破ってしまったりでは盗み見が露呈してしまうので、封の糊[のり]は湯気で溶かす。人として足らないところばかりであるのに、こういう悪知恵ばかり心得ているのが小面憎い。
lines.japaneseRuby: 言いつけられた仕事を大人しくこなすだけに留めればいいものを、朔屋は預けられた封書の中味に出歯亀根性抑えがたく、[R糊付^のりづ]けにされた封筒を開けてみようとしているのである。鋏を入れたり破ってしまったりでは盗み見が露呈してしまうので、封の糊[のり]は湯気で溶かす。人として足らないところばかりであるのに、こういう悪知恵ばかり心得ているのが小面憎い。
lines.english: He should have simply done as instructed. Instead, unable to curb his snooping curiosity about the letter entrusted to him, he was trying to open its glued flap. Cutting or tearing it would expose the intrusion. Steam would dissolve the glue. Deficient in almost every human quality, yet versed in such petty cunning: irritating indeed.

lines.japanese: 「ん、ならこいつをもらうよ。お幾らだい」
lines.english: “Hm. Then I'll have this. How much?”

lines.japanese: 亭主の咎めだてに、数十年の脂が現世の柵のように頼もしく染みついてべとついた屋台の、売り物に手を伸ばしてみたのだって半ば無意識だし、籠に並んで福々しい中華饅頭を器用に避けて、小皿につけあわせの搾菜なのだから恐れ入る。よく漬かって香がきついのを噛みながらには、さしもの亭主も眉が下がって、情けない。
lines.japaneseRuby: 亭主の咎めだてに、数十年の脂が現世の[R柵^しがらみ]のように頼もしく染みついてべとついた屋台の、売り物に手を伸ばしてみたのだって半ば無意識だし、籠に並んで福々しい中華饅頭を器用に避けて、小皿につけあわせの[R搾菜^ザアサイ]なのだから恐れ入る。よく漬かって香がきついのを噛みながらには、さしもの亭主も眉が下がって、情けない。
lines.english: Even reaching for something on sale in response to the owner's scolding was half unconscious. Decades of grease clung reassuringly to the stall, sticky as worldly entanglements. Yet his hand deftly avoided the cheerfully plump buns in their baskets and went instead to the pickled mustard stem served as a garnish on a small plate. Astonishing. As he chewed the pungent, well-pickled stuff, even the owner looked crestfallen.

lines.japanese: 「なんだかなあこの若僧は。付け合わせ一抓み囓って『勘定』もなにもあるもんかね……」
lines.japaneseRuby: 「なんだかなあこの若僧は。付け合わせ一[R抓^つま]み囓って『勘定』もなにもあるもんかね……」
lines.english: “What's with this young fellow? ‘How much,’ for a pinch of garnish?”

lines.japanese: 「大体、吝嗇が鰻屋の香気聴いて菜にするてぇなら落語だが。蒸籠の湯気を借りるなんて聞いたことないよ」
lines.japaneseRuby: 「大体、[R吝嗇^りんしょく]が鰻屋の[R香気^かざ]聴いて[R菜^さい]にするてぇなら落語だが。蒸籠の湯気を借りるなんて聞いたことないよ」
lines.english: “A miser using the smell of grilled eel as a side dish, that's a comic story. Never heard of someone borrowing a steamer's steam.”

lines.japanese: 「いやあこうやって同期のにやけ野郎に届いたラブレター、中味よく覗いたもんよ」
lines.english: “Oh, I used to snoop on love letters sent to a smarmy fellow in my year like this.”

lines.japanese: 「ついでに中味エロ小説まがいに書き換えて、すり替えてやったりとかな」
lines.english: “Sometimes I'd rewrite them like dirty novels and swap them in.”

lines.japanese: 「ちなみにそいつは後で婦女暴行犯として捕まったわけだが。差出人の女の子と逢った時、ナニ血迷ってナニやらかしたもんだか」
lines.english: “Incidentally, he got arrested for rape afterward. Met the girl who'd sent the letter and lost his head somehow. Who knows what he did.”

lines.japanese: 「兄さん、あんたひどいよ」
lines.english: “Brother, you're awful.”

lines.japanese: 「いいんだよ、仲間内でやってた賭け麻雀に大負けしたからって、サツに密告るような卑怯者だったんだから」
lines.japaneseRuby: 「いいんだよ、仲間内でやってた賭け麻雀に大負けしたからって、サツに[R密告^チク]るような卑怯者だったんだから」
lines.english: “Served him right. He was the kind of coward who lost heavily at our gambling mahjong, then informed on us to the cops.”

lines.japanese:
「……おお開いたぜえ。
　どれどれ───」
lines.english: “…Oh, it's open. Let's see—”

lines.japanese: 入っていたのは、端で破られた政府の臨時発行印紙一枚。それのみ。貨幣としては最低の価値しかない。ただその破れ目に何事か赤印の割り印が。
lines.english: Inside was a single stamp from a temporary government issue, torn along one edge. Nothing else. As currency it had only the lowest value. But along the tear was part of some red seal stamped across it.

lines.japanese: （なんだぁこりゃ）
lines.english: (What's this?)

lines.japanese: 何らかの書類ならともかく、半切れの印紙のみでは当てずっぽうもならず、困惑する朔屋を横目にして、店主は街路の向こうへ視線を流した。
lines.english: A document might have given him something to guess at. Half a stamp gave him nothing. As Sakuya puzzled over it, the owner glanced past him, across the street.

lines.japanese:
「まあなんだっていいんだけどさ。
　あんたいいのかい、あの白子の餓鬼、
　あんたの連れじゃないのかい？」
lines.english: “Whatever. But are you sure about that albino kid? Isn't she with you?”

lines.japanese: 見れば朔屋について下船してきたクロが、通りかかったチンドン屋の賑々しいのにふらふらとついて行ってしまったところ。
lines.english: He looked. Kuro, who had come ashore with him, was drifting off after a passing advertising band's noisy street procession.

lines.japanese:
「わあ、なんか楽しそう、面白そう。
　どこ行くのかな、なんかのお祭りかな。
　クロに教えて」
lines.japaneseRuby:
「わあ、なんか楽しそう、面白そう。
　どこ行くのかな、なんかのお祭りかな。
　クロに[R教^おせ]えて」
lines.english: “Wow, that looks fun. Interesting. Where are they going? Is it some festival? Tell Kuro.”

lines.japanese: 後先もなく、警戒もまるでなく、ハーメルンのネズミ取りに連れ去られていく子供のように遠ざかるクロを、朔屋、慌てて追いかけて襟首掴んで引き留めた。
lines.japaneseRuby: 後先もなく、警戒もまるでなく、ハーメルンのネズミ取りに連れ去られていく子供のように遠ざかるクロを、朔屋、慌てて追いかけて[R襟首^えりくび]掴んで引き留めた。
lines.english: Thoughtless and completely unguarded, Kuro receded like a child being carried away by the Pied Piper of Hamelin. Sakuya hurried after her and caught her by the collar.

lines.japanese:
「ああもう、ちょっとでも目を離しゃすぐこれだ。
　なんだってお前さんをつけてよこしたかな」
lines.english: “Oh, for crying out loud. Look away for a moment and there you go. Why'd they send you along?”

lines.japanese:
せっかく久しぶりの陸に降りて、あわよくば尻に帆掛けてとんずらのつもりの朔屋だったのに───
　何故かクロも共に付けられているとあっては。
　なんだって彼女がついてくるのか。朔屋が逃げてしまわないようにお目付役なのか。だとしても到底まともにこなせるとは思えないのだが。
　あるいは朔屋に対しての厭がらせ、なのだろうか。
　クロを連れて歩けば、要らぬ気疲れを強いられるのは間違いない。だが、本気でクロを見失ってそれっきり、という事だって充分にあり得る。
　いなくなっても構わない、そういう扱いという事かと、朔屋は、そぞろ哀れを催して軽くクロの頭を掌でぽんぽんぽん、愛叩してやろうとしたのに。
lines.japaneseRuby:
せっかく久しぶりの陸に降りて、あわよくば尻に帆掛けてとんずらのつもりの朔屋だったのに───
　何故かクロも共に付けられているとあっては。
　なんだって彼女がついてくるのか。朔屋が逃げてしまわないようにお目付役なのか。だとしても到底まともにこなせるとは思えないのだが。
　あるいは朔屋に対しての[R厭^いや]がらせ、なのだろうか。
　クロを連れて歩けば、要らぬ気疲れを強いられるのは間違いない。だが、本気でクロを見失ってそれっきり、という事だって充分にあり得る。
　いなくなっても構わない、そういう扱いという事かと、朔屋は、そぞろ哀れを催して軽くクロの頭を掌でぽんぽんぽん、[R愛叩^あいこう]してやろうとしたのに。
lines.english:
He had finally got ashore after so long, intending to flee at the slightest opportunity. Yet for some reason Kuro had been sent with him.
Why was she here? To watch him and prevent his escape? She hardly seemed capable of doing that properly.
Or was this harassment?
Walking around with her would undoubtedly exhaust him with unnecessary worry. But it was quite possible he might genuinely lose her and never see her again.
Did that mean they did not care if she disappeared? A little pity stirred him. He tried to give her head a few light, affectionate pats. But—

lines.japanese:
「ご、ごめっ、なぁさい……っ。
　もうしません、しないです、から。
　クロをぶたないで───」
lines.english: “S-sorry… I'm sorry… I won't do it again, I won't, so… Don't hit Kuro—”

lines.japanese: 白子の少女はひっと身を竦めて上目遣いの、浮かべてみせた笑みに、阿るような遜るような卑屈が滲んで、扱いに困り果てる朔屋だった。
lines.japaneseRuby: 白子の少女はひっと身を竦めて上目遣いの、浮かべてみせた笑みに、[R阿^おもね]るような[R遜^へりくだ]るような卑屈が滲んで、扱いに困り果てる朔屋だった。
lines.english: The albino girl shrank with a gasp and looked up at him. Her smile seeped with servility, flattering and abasing herself. Sakuya had no idea how to handle her.

lines.japanese: 夜闇が濃くなりまさるにつれ、港に通う風は足を緩めて滞留し、潮風に散らされる事なく、夜気に重油の匂いが蟠る。湾に突きだした堤防の先にて燈台がぐるぐると、回す一つ目の灯火は海上の残照の中ではまだ道化めいて白けているが、直に夜航の船の心強い導き手となろう。夜番を運良く免れた水夫は、ロッカーに隠しておいた上陸用の糊[のり]の利いた襯衣に袖[そで]を通し、筋や骨を軋ませる、一日の苦役の疲労を港湾労働者達は肩を回して散らしながら、それぞれのお定まりの飯屋や酒場目指して街方へと流れていく。

lines.english: As darkness deepened, the wind crossing the port slowed and lingered. Without the sea breeze to disperse it, the smell of heavy oil coiled in the night air. At the end of a breakwater projecting into the bay, a lighthouse turned its single eye round and round. Against the last light on the sea, it still looked foolish and ineffectual. Soon it would become a reassuring guide to ships sailing at night. Sailors lucky enough to avoid the night watch slipped into starched shore-going shirts hidden in their lockers. Dockworkers rolled their shoulders to dispel a day's fatigue, muscles and bones creaking. Each drifted toward the streets and his usual eating house or tavern.

lines.japanese: 船から港へ、港から街路へ、移動していく喧噪に逆らって人気の失せつつある港湾倉庫群を目指す二人がある。流れに逆行して、というて木の間を躱す燕のように、とは軽敏にいかない。撞球台に放たれた持ち玉よろしくあちらの荒くれにぶつかっては手荒に弾き飛ばされ、こちらの無頼の前によろばいでては跳ね返されてと、撲ち身の一つ二つこさえながら、それでも二人は遅れを取り戻そうとの必死さ滲む。正確には、連れの一方ばかりが焦っていたのであるが。
lines.japaneseRuby: 船から港へ、港から街路へ、移動していく喧噪に逆らって[R人気^ひとけ]の失せつつある港湾倉庫群を目指す二人がある。流れに逆行して、というて木の間を[R躱^かわ]す燕のように、とは軽敏にいかない。[R撞球^ビリヤード]台に放たれた持ち玉よろしくあちらの荒くれにぶつかっては手荒に弾き飛ばされ、こちらの無頼の前によろばいでては跳ね返されてと、[R撲^う]ち身の一つ二つこさえながら、それでも二人は遅れを取り戻そうとの必死さ滲む。正確には、連れの一方ばかりが焦っていたのであるが。
lines.english: Against the moving clamor—from ships to port, from port to streets—two people headed toward the increasingly deserted warehouses. Going against the current did not mean darting lightly like swallows between trees. More like a cue ball sent across a billiard table: hitting a roughneck here and bouncing away, stumbling before a ruffian there and being knocked back. Acquiring a bruise or two, they nevertheless showed a desperate effort to make up lost time. Strictly speaking, only one of them was desperate.

lines.japanese:
「まずいなぁ……すっかり暗くなっちまった。
　クロぉ、お前がもたもたしてるからだぜ」
lines.english: “This is bad… It's completely dark. Kuro, it's because you keep dawdling.”

lines.japanese:
「だって、サアカスだったもの。
　きょういの、ええと……千里、眼と、
　しじょう最高の、軽業って。
　いた、いたい、引っぱっちゃやぁ」
lines.japaneseRuby:
「だって、サアカスだったもの。
　きょういの、ええと……千里、眼と、
　しじょう最高の、[R軽業^かるわざ]って。
　いた、いたい、引っぱっちゃやぁ」
lines.english: “But it was a circus. Amazing, um… clair… voyance, and the greatest acrobatics ever. Ow, ow, don't pull…”

lines.japanese:
「何がサアカスなもんだかな。
　お前なんぞそんなとこのこのこ首突っこんだらたちまち攫[さら]われる」
lines.english: “What circus? Poke your nose into a place like that and they'll carry you off straightaway.”

lines.japanese:
「奥羽山中の『六尺のオオイタチ（大板血）』とか、ブルネイ渡りの『毛達磨男』に混じって、親の因果が子に報いの『白子娘』でござぁいと、たちまち丸盆前座にされちまうのがオチだぁ。
　……ああすいませんね、こいつ、ちっとばかりとろいもんで」
lines.japaneseRuby:
「奥羽山中の『六尺のオオイタチ（大板血）』とか、[Rブルネイ^ボルネオ]渡りの『毛達磨男』に混じって、親の因果が子に報いの『白子娘』でござぁいと、たちまち丸盆前座にされちまうのがオチだぁ。
　……ああすいませんね、こいつ、ちっとばかりとろいもんで」
lines.english:
“With the ‘Six-Foot Giant Weasel’ from the Ou mountains—a big board stained with blood—and the ‘Hairy Human Ball’ from Borneo, it'll be ‘Behold the albino girl, her parents' sins visited upon their child!’ They'll have you on a round sideshow stage as the opening act before you know it.
…Oh, excuse us. She's a bit slow.”

lines.japanese:
今もどんと肩ぶっつけ合った港男達に、いい加減な詫び文句で割って入ってクロを背に隠す。
　白子の娘の、乳白の髪、肌と血凝りのような目の色は夜目にも悪目立ちして、歩みを遮[さえぎ]られた港男達の奇異の眼差しが、クロの哀れな様子に嗜虐催し意地悪な悪戯を企んで歪みかねないその前に、と乱暴に手を引いて引き離しつ、朔屋のぼやきはいささか責任転嫁の。
lines.english:
They had just collided shoulder-first with more harbor men. He gave a careless apology, inserted himself between them, and hid Kuro behind his back.
Her milk-white hair and skin, her blood-clot-colored eyes, stood out badly even in the dark. Before the men whose passage they had blocked could let their curious looks twist into cruel mischief at her pitiful appearance, he roughly pulled her away. His grumbling shifted the blame a little.

lines.japanese:
チンドン屋についていった後で、町外れの曲馬団の呼びこみに、ふらふら引かれていって迷子になりかけたのはクロであるが、朔屋だって道中で見かけた豊満美女に、一時の火遊びを気取ってかき口説いたりで寄り道した。
　乳と尻ばかりに栄養がいったような女が地回りの情婦とかで、小指の欠けて刺青もんもんの腕で絞め殺そうになったところをほうほうの態で逃げ延びたという時間喰らいの顛末もあったり、まったくクロを笑えぬ穀潰しな。

　乳と尻ばかりに栄養がいったような女が地回りの[R情婦^イロ]とかで、小指の欠けて刺青もんもんの腕で絞め殺そうになったところをほうほうの態で逃げ延びたという時間喰らいの顛末もあったり、まったくクロを笑えぬ穀潰しな。
lines.english:
Kuro had followed the advertising band, then drifted toward a circus barker on the edge of town and nearly got lost. But Sakuya had made detours himself, trying to seduce a voluptuous beauty he met along the way as though embarking upon a little affair.
The woman, whose nourishment seemed to have gone entirely to breasts and backside, turned out to be a local gangster's mistress. A tattooed arm with a missing little finger nearly strangled him; his scrambling escape had consumed time, too. A useless mouth who could hardly laugh at Kuro.

lines.japanese: こうして朔屋達が指定の倉庫に辿り着いた時は、かく益体のない寄り道回り道で時間を食いつぶし、刻限を時計一巡りほども遅れた頃であったとか。朔屋は倉庫に駆けずりこむ前に、小賢しくも髪を鳥の巣にかき回し服のあちこち乱し港の油混じりの土埃塗りたくって『さっき、通関の檻から逃げ出した大食蟻獣に襲われてしまい必死に逃げ出して来たのでまことに遺憾ながら遅れてしまいました』の風を装ったところ、取引相手から怒りを通り越した、犬の糞にたかる蝿でも見るような目線を送られ、小芝居も完膚無きまで無視されたという。

lines.english: By the time they reached the designated warehouse, such pointless detours had wasted enough time to make them a whole turn of the clock behind schedule, or so the story goes. Before rushing inside, Sakuya cunningly tousled his hair into a bird's nest, disordered his clothes, and smeared himself with the port's oily dirt. His performance suggested: ‘A giant anteater escaped from its customs cage and attacked me. I fled desperately, so regrettably I am late.’ His counterpart's look, however, had gone beyond anger. It was the look one gives flies swarming on dog shit. The little performance was utterly ignored.

lines.japanese:
大体朔屋も始めから、相手を見て冗談が通じるような相手かどうか悟るべき。がらんと積み荷も乏しいのに薄汚れて荒廃の気色濃い倉庫の中で、その男だけは塵一つ被っていなかった。それも自分で払うのではなく、奴隷の躾[しつけ]叩きこんだメイド任せに羽根箒で浄めさせる手合いで、白く眩しいマオカラーで上下隆と揃え、糸くず一つさえ見えないくらいにブラシのしっかりかかって、仕立てもよろしく袖[そで]から肩口を思いきり引っぱっても、すぐに皺一つなく戻るであろう。
　面差しはそれなりに整っていたけれど、搾取に慣れた者に特有の傲慢が目に溜まる。ただその支配相は代々の青い血に篆刻されたものではないとは見えて、人を不快にさせる、卑しくにやけ加減で口角が歪む。さして観相術の心得を持ち合わせない朔屋にも容易く察せられる、こいつは───成金だ。

lines.english:
Sakuya should have recognized at first sight whether this was a man who appreciated jokes. The warehouse was filthy and desolate despite its emptiness and scant cargo. The man alone bore not a speck of dust. Nor would he brush it off himself: he was the sort to have a maid trained into slavery dust him with a feather brush. His brilliant white, Mao-collared suit was immaculately matched above and below, brushed free of even a loose thread. The tailoring was excellent. Pull sleeve or shoulder as hard as you liked, and it would probably return without a wrinkle.
His face was reasonably handsome. But his eyes held the arrogance peculiar to those accustomed to exploitation. The stamp of dominance seemed not to have been engraved through generations of blue blood. Something base and smirking twisted the corners of his mouth, making him unpleasant. Even Sakuya, with little skill in reading faces, could readily tell: this was new money.

lines.japanese: だからといって舐めて居丈高に掛かれる相手ではない事を言葉を交わす前に感じ取ったのは、朔屋にしてからが権勢に弱く強きにへつらう軟弱者であったから。たとい先代かそこらで歩がひっくり返ったような金満であろうと金の力の灼かなること言うまでもないし、何よりその成金……おほん、そのぽっと出のお大尽……もとい、富豪の両脇には、矜羯羅・制多迦の両童子の如く、屈強な男二人が固めていたからである。ダークスーツにボルサリーノ、灰色の襯衣に青のタイは見ようによっては粋と言えたが、コミニュケーションと言えば言語より暴力を重視すること間違いなしの粗暴で野卑な面相からして、下品なチンピラ、という枠からは外れない……なにが不動の脇侍どころか、地獄の獄卒、牛頭馬頭がいいところ。

lines.english: Yet even before they exchanged words, he sensed this was no one to treat with contempt or bluster. Sakuya himself was a weakling before power, cringing toward the strong. Even if a pawn had been promoted into this wealth only in the previous generation, money's force was undeniable. Above all, on either side of the upstart—hem, the suddenly prosperous grandee—rather, the wealthy gentleman—stood two powerful men, guarding him like Kongara and Seitaka. Dark suits and Borsalino hats; gray shirts and blue ties. Seen one way, they might have been stylish. But their crude, brutal faces left no doubt that they preferred violence to language as a means of communication. They never escaped the category of vulgar hoodlum. Fudo's attendants? Hardly. Hell's Ox-Head and Horse-Face were closer.

lines.japanese: どれだけ身なりよろしく整えたところで、やはりというか所詮というか、海の厄介者信天翁号の取引相手にはお差し合いの、これは、やくざ者かギャングの類だ、根本を、信天翁号の面々が日頃からシノギを見苦しく奪い合っている外道と同じところに置いている。
lines.english: However well dressed, they were ultimately appropriate counterparts for that maritime menace, the Albatross. Yakuza or gangsters. Their foundations lay in the same place as the scoundrels with whom the Albatross's company so sordidly competed for a living.

lines.speakerEn: Rich Man in a White Suit
lines.japanese: 「遅いな。いい歳をして使いもまともに出来ないような役立たずを寄越すあたり、お前の船の面子も底が知れる」
lines.english: “You're late. Sending a useless fellow who can't run an errand properly at his age tells me all I need to know about your ship's company.”

lines.speakerEn: Rich Man in a White Suit
lines.japanese: 「いや……あの信天翁号にまともな『商取引』を期待する方が酷、か。どれだけ粋がったところで、所詮は居場所もない愚連隊もどきだからな、信天翁の奴らは。噂通りだな───」
lines.english: “No… Perhaps expecting a proper ‘business transaction’ from the Albatross is itself unfair. Whatever airs they put on, they're merely a gang of delinquents with nowhere to belong. Just as the rumors say—”

lines.japanese: 駆け足の、荒い息を押さえようとする朔屋をさも見苦しげに一瞥し、居丈高に言い放ってから口元に宛がった飾り入りの手巾で語尾が曇った、罵倒の文句には苛立ちと怒りが見やすい。普段から、埃と悪臭の籠もるがままに放置された廃倉庫に尊大なる身を待たされた事に対しての不快の念だろうが、それだけではないと朔屋は不審を覚[おぼ]ゆる。怒りに尖る眼差しには滑るような油光りも入り交じり、それは恐らくは渇望の心。こういう手合いは相手を下と認識すれば、目を合わせるどころか洟[はな]も引っかけない傲慢さを示すものだが、この男、どうにも目の端でちらちらと朔屋達に欲色の視線をよこしてきているのだ。

lines.english: He glanced disdainfully at Sakuya, still trying to catch his breath after running, and spoke with haughty force. An ornamental handkerchief raised to his mouth muffled the ending. Irritation and anger showed plainly in the abuse. Displeasure at having his exalted person kept waiting in an abandoned warehouse, left to accumulate dust and stench. Yet Sakuya suspected something more. Amid the angry sharpness of his eyes gleamed an oily shine. Probably longing. Men of this sort usually deemed others beneath them and would not so much as meet their eyes or spit at them. This one kept casting sidelong, covetous glances their way.

lines.japanese:
ははぁん奴さん、こう豪くお冠なのも、実のところこの取引とやらに余程ご執心だったからと見える───とそう、つけいる隙になりそうなと見るや目端が利いてくるあたり、朔屋も中途半端に狭っ辛い。
　もちろんそんな得心はおくびにも出さず、なにしろお大尽自体は朔屋と似たり寄ったりな線の細さではあるとはいえ、両脇に控えた手下が恐ろしい、差し出口は呑みこんだ。ただでさえ船の上では余計な一言多くして、吊されたり絞められたり畳まれたりしている彼である。

lines.english:
Aha. Perhaps he was so furious because he badly wanted whatever this deal offered. The moment Sakuya saw a possible opening, his eyes grew sharp. He possessed a half-baked cunning of his own.
Of course, he betrayed none of that understanding. The grandee himself was thinly built, much like Sakuya, but the men attending him were frightening. He swallowed his unnecessary remarks. On the ship, too, one word too many was forever getting him strung up, throttled, or folded in half.

lines.japanese:
「いやその、ホントすんません。
　来る途中で色々ありまして。
　で、それで僕は、何をすればいいんでしょうか」
lines.english: “No, um, I'm really sorry. Various things happened on the way. So, what am I supposed to do?”

lines.japanese: 「なんしろ僕は、ただここで貴方がたに会ってこいと、それしか言われてないもんでして」
lines.english: “All I was told was to come here and meet you.”

lines.japanese: 殊更阿呆を装うまでもなく、朔屋は本当にそれだけの指示しか受け取っておらず、こんな裏ぶれた事この上ない倉庫でなにをしようというのか、見当もつかないのだ。朔屋が預かった物は例の封書の一つのみ、向こうだって空手で、倉庫には取引に供するような荷らしい物は見当たらない。それどころか倉庫は床にかつての荷箱の痕と思しい線を寒々しく残して寂しく広く、往時は満載になった事もあろうし、立ち働く人足の出入りに忙しなかった有り様が忍ばれるだけに、現在の侘びしさと言ったらなかった。荒れているのは信天翁号も同じだが、あちらは開き直ったようなふてぶてしささえ漂わせているのに、この倉庫と来たら、巨大な髑髏の歯欠け落ちた口腔に立ったような嘘寒ささえ感じさせるでないか。

lines.english: He need not especially pretend to be a fool. Those really were all the instructions he had received, and he could not imagine what they meant to do in this supremely run-down warehouse. He had only the one envelope. The other party was empty-handed, too. No cargo suitable for a transaction was in sight. Indeed, the floor retained only forlorn outlines where crates had once stood, leaving a cold, lonely expanse. One could imagine the old days, filled with goods and busy with laborers coming and going. That made the present desolation all the worse. The Albatross was equally decrepit, but she possessed a brazen air of having embraced it. This warehouse made him feel the eerie chill of standing in the toothless mouth of a gigantic skull.

lines.japanese:
「本当に子供の使いと同じだなお前は。
　……まあいい。書類を預かってるだろう」
lines.english: “You really are no better than a child sent on an errand. Never mind. You have some papers, don't you?”

lines.japanese: 手下の一人に顎で示して朔屋へと差し向ける、どすどすと本人は威圧のつもりか、下品なまでに磨き上げたエナメルの靴で汚れた足元わざわざ音高く、鳴らして寄ってきたで案の定埃が舞い上がって、煙幕じみた霞に裸電球の光線がサーチライトの光条じみる。もとよりその書類しか持ち合わせていない朔屋は、鼻腔を犯す埃の粒子に閉口し、内心で毒づきながら手渡す封書の、ただ預かってきただけ、中味に興味など鼻糞ほどもないとあっさりと（封は糊[のり]に唾して閉じ直してあった）。
lines.english: A jerk of the chin sent one henchman toward him. Perhaps intending intimidation, the fellow loudly stamped through the dirt in patent-leather shoes polished to vulgar brilliance. Predictably, dust rose. In the smoke-screen haze, rays from the naked bulbs looked like searchlight beams. Sakuya had nothing but the document in any case. Irritated by the dust invading his nose, he cursed inwardly and casually handed over the envelope. Merely entrusted with it; not a speck of interest in its contents. He had spat on the glue and resealed it.

lines.japanese: 「旦那、こちらです」
lines.english: “Here it is, sir.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 鷹揚に受け取って、葉巻の端切り用のナイフを内ポケットからぱちり、封を切る手は大人を気取っていかにもな勿体つけを、装って、微妙な焦りが浮いてやしないか。それのみならず、やはりこちらを覗き見しているようなが朔屋の気にかかる。というよりその目線が捕らえているのは───クロ？
lines.english: He accepted it with a grand air, snapped a cigar-cutting knife from an inner pocket, and slit the envelope. His hands affected an ostentatiously mature deliberation. Wasn't there a little impatience beneath it? And again, Sakuya was bothered by the apparent covert glances. Or rather, what those eyes were watching was—Kuro?

lines.japanese:
先程からやけに大人しい。街中でもこうだったらなんの苦労もないのに、この小娘、あれは俺を困らせようと思ってか、嫌がらせかと逆捩じの朔屋、あのお大尽も一体こんな貧相な小娘に何を見ているのだと、倉庫に入ってからようやく初めてクロに目を向けたのだが。
　肩が細かく震えていた。
　顔が、藁半紙でも丸めたようにそれはそれはくしゃくしゃに崩れていた。

lines.english:
She had been remarkably quiet. Had she behaved like this in town, there would have been no trouble. Had all that been deliberate, to annoy him? Sakuya twisted matters perversely. What did the grandee see in such a miserable little girl? For the first time since entering the warehouse, he turned his eyes to her.
Her shoulders trembled minutely.
Her face was crumpled, utterly crumpled, like balled-up pulp paper.

lines.japanese: 胡椒を叩きつけられた狆だってこうはいかないとぎょっとして、思わず一歩下がった朔屋の前でクロは、遂に臨界を超えて、身が二つ折りになった、白髪が舞い踊る、弾けた音が───
lines.japaneseRuby: 胡椒を叩きつけられた[R狆^チン]だってこうはいかないとぎょっとして、思わず一歩下がった朔屋の前でクロは、遂に臨界を超えて、身が二つ折りになった、白髪が舞い踊る、弾けた音が───
lines.english: Not even a Japanese chin pelted with pepper could have managed that. Startled, Sakuya stepped back. Before him, Kuro finally passed her critical point and doubled over. White hair flew. The sound burst out—

lines.japanese: 「ひゃああっっっくしょーーんっっ！」
lines.english: “Hyaaaa-CHOO!”

lines.japanese:
手下が蹴立てた埃は背丈だけは人並みにある朔屋さえ煙たがらせたのだから、クロなど推して知るべしで、強かに吸いこんでいたのだろう、鼻腔をこれでもかとくすぐられていたのだろう、くしゃみは小柄な体が張り裂けそうなほど強烈にやかましく、同時に鼻痒さからの解放に爽快ですら、の、ただしこれははたで聞いている者にとってはで、クロとしては爽快どころではなかった、それどころでは。
　くしゃみは潔く抜けていくだけに留まらず、喉に絡まって彼女を咳きこませ、

手下が蹴立てた埃は背丈だけは人並みにある朔屋さえ煙たがらせたのだから、クロなど推して知るべしで、[R強^したた]かに吸いこんでいたのだろう、鼻腔をこれでもかとくすぐられていたのだろう、くしゃみは小柄な体が張り裂けそうなほど強烈にやかましく、同時に鼻[R痒^がゆ]さからの解放に爽快ですら、の、ただしこれははたで聞いている者にとってはで、クロとしては爽快どころではなかった、それどころでは。
　くしゃみは潔く抜けていくだけに留まらず、喉に絡まって彼女を咳きこませ、
lines.english:
The dust kicked up by the henchman had bothered even Sakuya, who at least had an ordinary person's height. One could imagine what it did to Kuro. She must have inhaled a great deal. It must have tickled her nose beyond endurance. The sneeze was so fierce and loud that her little body seemed ready to split. The release from that itching was almost refreshing—to a listener, that is. For Kuro it was nothing of the kind. Far from it.
The sneeze did not simply pass cleanly out. It caught in her throat and made her cough—

lines.japanese:
「っ!?　え、ふ、こほ……コふッ、
　コン……っ」
lines.english: “!? Eh, fuh, cohh… Cough… Coh…”

lines.japanese: 崩れてぺたりと手をついた床は、また埃まみれで咳をさらに激しくし、
lines.english: She collapsed, palms flat on the floor. More dust. Her coughing grew worse.

lines.japanese: 「……ふっ、こほ、ん、んっ、んぅ～……？」
lines.english: “…Fuh, cough, mm, mm, mmm…?”

lines.japanese: ……出口のない圧力が体内を暴れ回る苦痛は、便秘や胃酸過多に苦しむ持病持ちなら共感してくれるだろう。しかもそれらの苦痛は漸増的に高まっていくのに、今回のクロは突然のくしゃみによる、突発的で自家中毒的な内圧である。それも高圧の。見ているうちに、蹲ったクロのほつれ髪から覗くうなじや耳朶が赤くなるやら青くなるやら目まぐるしく、焦って朔屋は抱き起こして、少女の頬が向日葵の種を一杯に詰め込んだ天竺鼠よろしく膨れあがり、唇懸命に食いしばっているのに、起こさなければよかったと、返す手で反射的に突き飛ばしたのがなんともはや、酷いというか仕方ない反応というか、ともかくそれが止めとなり、堤防を崩す、最後の一突きとなり。
lines.japaneseRuby: ……出口のない圧力が体内を暴れ回る苦痛は、便秘や胃酸過多に苦しむ持病持ちなら共感してくれるだろう。しかもそれらの苦痛は漸増的に高まっていくのに、今回のクロは突然のくしゃみによる、突発的で自家中毒的な内圧である。それも高圧の。見ているうちに、[R蹲^うずくま]ったクロのほつれ髪から覗くうなじや[R耳朶^じだ]が赤くなるやら青くなるやら目まぐるしく、焦って朔屋は抱き起こして、少女の頬が向日葵の種を一杯に詰め込んだ天竺鼠よろしく膨れあがり、唇懸命に食いしばっているのに、起こさなければよかったと、返す手で反射的に突き飛ばしたのがなんともはや、[R酷^むご]いというか仕方ない反応というか、ともかくそれが[R止^とど]めとなり、堤防を崩す、最後の一突きとなり。
lines.english: …Those with chronic constipation or excess stomach acid might sympathize with the agony of pressure raging inside with no way out. But their suffering rose gradually. Kuro's was a sudden, self-poisoning internal pressure brought on by the sneeze. High pressure, too. As they watched, the neck and ears visible through her loosened hair changed rapidly from red to blue. Alarmed, Sakuya lifted her. Her cheeks had swollen like a guinea pig's stuffed with sunflower seeds. Her lips were desperately clenched. He should not have picked her up. His returning hands reflexively shoved her away. Cruel, or an understandable reaction? Either way, it finished the matter. The last push that broke the dam.

lines.japanese: 「ぅぇぁぁぁああ～～～っっっ」
lines.english: “Uweaaaaah…”

lines.japanese: 体力に乏しいクロの身に、ここまで街中を無駄にふらついたり朔屋に無理矢理走らされたりで相当の負荷がかかっていたのが災いしたのだろうかとか、小賢しい分析などまさに反吐でも喰らえで、最初の一吹きで反吐は床の上に埃その他の堆積物と混ざり合った目出度い混淆の液溜まりを為し、続く第二波第三波が湿った音と共に版図を広げ、
lines.japaneseRuby: 体力に乏しいクロの身に、ここまで街中を無駄にふらついたり朔屋に無理矢理走らされたりで相当の負荷がかかっていたのが災いしたのだろうかとか、小賢しい分析などまさに反吐でも喰らえで、最初の一吹きで反吐は床の上に埃その他の堆積物と混ざり合った目出度い[R混淆^こんこう]の液溜まりを為し、続く第二波第三波が湿った音と共に版図を広げ、
lines.english: Perhaps Kuro's slight strength had been overtaxed by all the useless wandering in town and the running Sakuya forced upon her. Such clever analysis could swallow vomit. The first eruption made a splendidly mixed puddle of vomit, dust, and other accumulated matter on the floor. A second and third wave spread its territory with wet sounds—

lines.japanese: 「うぇ、えぶっ、むーーーーっ」
lines.english: “Ueh, ebuh, mmmm…”

lines.japanese:
衝き上がるえづきの苦しみに目がほとんど白目に裏返り、クロはぶるぶると悶えながら自ら広げた小間物屋（隠語的表現）に顔から倒れ伏していく、その襟首を引き留めた手は、頼もしい、誰あろう、朔屋───などであろうか、多くの殴る蹴るを経て拳胼胝などでごつごつしているから彼ではない、なんと取引相手の手下の一人。二重の意味で呆気にとられた朔屋には構いもせず、甲斐甲斐しく少女の口元を拭い、どういう気まぐれで慈悲を示すのか、またどういう心づもりでてきぱきと、どこからか取り出した六尺棒にクロの手足を縛りつけていくのか。両の手首を一つにくくりつけ、両脚を膝の裏で戒めて、出来上がった形は、仕留めた狸を棒に縛りつけて担いでいく時のそれ。
　そのままずるずる引きずって行くのがボスの下へ、部下の突然の暴走に金持ちは度を失う、でもなく、むしろ喜色で頷[うなず]いた。

lines.english: The surge of retching (tsuki) rolled his eyes nearly all the way back, and Kuro, shuddering and thrashing, face-planted into the “knick-knack shop” (slang expression) he’d spread himself. The hand that seized his collar (erikubi) was—reassuringly—Sakuya’s— or so one might think—but after all the punching and kicking, his hands were rough and calloused from the blows, so it couldn’t be him. To her surprise, it was one of her business partner’s henchmen. Paying no heed to Sakuya, who was dumbfounded in two ways, the man diligently wiped the girl’s mouth. By what whim was he showing mercy? And with what intent did he so efficiently tie Kuro’s limbs to a six-shaku staff he’d produced from somewhere? He lashed both wrists together, then bound the legs behind the knees; the pose looked like a caught raccoon dog strung on a pole. He dragged her off toward the boss. The rich man didn’t stutter at his underling’s sudden outburst—he nodded, grinning.

lines.japanese:
「よぅーしそうだ。それでいい。
　いきなり戻したのには面食らったが───」
lines.english: “All right, that’s it. That’s good enough. I was taken aback when you suddenly brought it back, though—”

lines.japanese: 「それもまたそそるなぁ、クロくん」
lines.english: “That’s pretty tempting too, Kuro-kun.”

lines.japanese: ……訳もわからないうちに、荒廃した倉庫という背景が、ボッシュなる幻視者がものした異端的な宗教画とも迷妄の一大産物ともつかぬ世界にすり替わったかの失墜感で眩暈しながら、朔屋は左右を見て、前後を見て、それでも受け入れきる事は出来ずに間抜けた笑み口元に張りつかせて呟いた。
lines.japaneseRuby: ……訳もわからないうちに、荒廃した倉庫という背景が、ボッシュなる幻視者がものした異端的な宗教画とも迷妄の一大産物ともつかぬ世界にすり替わったかの失墜感で[R眩暈^めまい]しながら、朔屋は左右を見て、前後を見て、それでも受け入れきる事は出来ずに間抜けた笑み口元に張りつかせて呟いた。
lines.english: …Before he knew it, the backdrop of the dilapidated warehouse had shifted into a world that felt replaced—a world that was indistinguishable from either a heretical religious painting by the visionary Bosch or a massive product of delusion. Dizzy from this sense of disorientation, Sakuya looked left and right, then front and back. Still unable to fully accept it, he muttered with a dazed smile frozen on his lips.

lines.japanese: 「ええと、これ、どういうこと？」
lines.english: “Um, what does this mean?”

lines.japanese: 「どういう事もなにも」
lines.english: “What do you mean, ‘what do you mean’?”

lines.japanese: 本人としては獲得せし者の余裕のつもりかもしれない微笑には、朔屋にもよくよく覚えがあった。曖昧宿にしけこんだ街娼の、パンツを引きずり下ろしていく時に自然に湧きあがる笑みと同質で、部屋の隅の姿見に映った己の鼻の下の長さに慌てて口元引き締めてももう遅い、娼婦にはしっかり見られてついでに足元も見られた様子だが、それでもその晩は二度・三度と浅ましく励んでそれは閑却、白スーツが渇望していた品とは、どうやら。

lines.english: Sakuya recognized that smile—the smirk of a victor, probably. It was the same kind of smile that rose when he pulled down a streetwalker’s panties in some seedy inn—and even if he clamped his lips tight the moment he spotted the line under his nose in the full-length mirror, it was already too late. The whore had seen him clear, and while she was at it she’d taken a look at his feet too. Still, he went at it two or three times that night—but setting that aside, it seems the item the man in the white suit had been craving was, after all...

lines.japanese: 「けふぅ……ああ、クロ、げろしちゃった」
lines.english: “Kefu… Ah, Kuro, I threw up.”

lines.japanese: 胃液臭いおくびを漏らして一息ついてから、
lines.english: She belched stomach acid and took a breath,

lines.japanese:
「あれ？　どうして、しばってるです？
　クロは、ごめんなさい、また粗相したから？
　クロ、ゲロしちゃったから？」
lines.english: “Huh? Why am I tied up? Is it because Kuro—sorry—messed up again? Is it because Kuro threw up?”

lines.japanese: ようやく把握した状況に混乱するというより、粗相への仕置きを恐れてわななく口元というのがまたこの白子の少女の卑屈さ加減を物語る。そして白スーツは、幼子の哀しい涙を吸いあげて滋養と為す妖魔のようにクロの困惑の顔を満悦の相で味わいつ、封書の中味を指先で摘[つま]み示すがディレイクション仕掛ける手品師はだしに大仰に。
lines.english: Rather than being confused by the situation she’d finally grasped, the fact that her lips trembled in fear of punishment for her mistake speaks volumes about this white-haired girl’s servile nature. And the woman in the white suit, like a demon that absorbs a child’s sad tears and turns them into nourishment, savored Kuro’s bewildered expression with a look of sheer delight, then pointed to the contents of the sealed envelope with her fingertips—but she did so with the exaggerated manner of a magician setting up a diversion.

lines.japanese: 「ようし。これでこの白子ちゃんは、僕のモノだなっ」
lines.english: “All right. With this, this little white kid’s mine now!”
“Huh!?”

lines.japanese: 「まあ知らなかったようだが、お前が持ってきた半券は、その子の身請け証文に張る印紙の片割れだったんだね」
lines.english: “Hey, you didn’t know, but that ticket stub you brought was actually half of the revenue stamp on that girl’s redemption certificate.”

lines.japanese:
知らぬで当たり前、展開を呑みこみかねて喉につまらせてくぐもった鼻息で返す朔屋に、白スーツが取り出す半券の片割れ、破れ目はぴたりと合い、割り印も重なった。厭になるほど気取って俗物臭い手さばきでは、種明かしもなにも、鼻につくばかり。
　ただし本人は観客の反応なぞ知った事かと大満足の、話していくうちに、目が狂的かつ偏執的なかぎろい垂れ流し、所作の度に厭らしい光跡を倉庫の暗がりに曳くかのよう、口調までも幼児的に躁を帯びる。

lines.english:
No surprise there—Sakuya, choking on the turn of events, replied with a muffled snort. The man in the white suit pulled out the other half of the ticket stub; the tears lined up perfectly, and the stamp marks aligned exactly. With a manner so pretentious and vulgar it was downright repulsive, the reveal—or whatever it was—was nothing but an annoyance.
　Yet the man—oblivious to the audience’s reaction and utterly satisfied—kept talking, his eyes streaming a frenzied, paranoid glare, and with every movement he seemed to trail a repulsive trail of light through the darkness of the warehouse; even his tone took on a childishly manic quality.

lines.japanese:
ああ───もしかして。
　こいつは、そういう───
　金持て余した馬鹿にありがちな、
　そういう───
lines.english: Ah—could it be? This guy is… that kind of— the kind of thing you often see with rich idiots who don’t know what to do with their money, that kind of—

lines.japanese:
衣食住共に満たされた人間が求めるものといっては、珍奇な刺激物というのが腐れた世の常の、より珍奇に、より新しいものと求めるうちに、日々の暮らしに追われる小市民には考えも及ばぬゲテモノ探求の道に踏みこんでいくのもありがちの。まあ考えてみれば確かに、珍味美味と称される馬鹿馬鹿しい程に高価な食物などにも、正体を聞けば鼻梁に嫌悪の皺寄せたくなるような物も多い。
　うらなりの白子で知恵足らずというどうしようもないクロなど、朔屋の食指を運ばせるには肉も水気も足らないが、世には進んでイカ物食いに手を染める輩もいる、そういう事だ。
lines.english: The well-fed, well-clothed, and well-housed are always craving the next odd thrill, and they keep pushing farther, into grotesqueries the nine-to-fivers can’t even dream of. Come to think of it, it’s certainly true that even among foods hailed as delicacies—ridiculously expensive ones—there are many whose true nature, once revealed, would make one wrinkle one’s nose in disgust. A hopeless fool like Kuro, who’s not exactly the sharpest tool in the shed, might not have enough meat or moisture to pique Sakuya’s appetite, but there are people in this world who willingly dabble in eating squid-based delicacies—that’s just how it is.

lines.japanese: 朔屋の想像を裏づけるように、身振り手振りの思い入れたっぷりに男は、スーツの白は変わらず清潔なのに、どこかしら濁りを帯びた。
lines.english: As if to confirm Sakuya’s suspicion, the man—gesturing passionately—seemed to take on a somewhat murky quality, even though the white of his suit remained as clean as ever.

lines.japanese:
「以前より噂は聞いていたんだね。
　あのボロ船の白子ちゃんのことはさ。
　小っちゃくって痩せっぽちで、
　その上舌っ足らずでお馬鹿って言うじゃないか」
lines.english: “I’d heard the gossip, you know. That Shirako-chan on the rickety tub. Tiny, skinny, and they say she stutters and isn’t too bright, right?”

lines.japanese: 「───なぁお前っっ!!」
lines.english: “Hey, you!!”

lines.japanese: 「おわあっ!?」
lines.english: “Whoa!?”

lines.japanese: 「ひぃ！」
lines.english: “Eek!”

Not only Sakuya—who was pointed at by the sweeping arc of his arm—but even Kuro, right in the blast of the deafening roar, quietly lost a few drops of urine. Had he noticed that, the man would surely have rejoiced even more ecstatically.

lines.japanese:
「そんな逸材、いませんよ!?
　僕は『小公女』とか『ああ無情』が大好きな子だった。でも僕が好きだったのは、最後に主人公の彼女達が救われるからじゃない」
lines.english: “No such prodigy exists! I was the type who loved A Little Princess and Les Misérables. But I liked them because the heroines were saved in the end.”

lines.japanese: 「むしろ救われるその瞬間には本を破り捨てたね。僕は彼女達が零落して落魄して、いじめられていじめ抜かれる事にうっとりしていたんだ」
lines.english: “The second I was saved, I tore the book to shreds. I was entranced, watching them fall, watching them get ground down, bullied, bullied, bullied.”

lines.japanese:
「いや、昂奮していたと言っていい。
　僕の春の目覚めは、彼女達の悲惨に導かれたって訳さ───なのに」
lines.english: “No, I was excited. My spring awakening came from their misery—and yet…”

lines.japanese:
「なんで最後に救われてしまうんだようっ。
　頭も成長も足らない女の子が、虐げられてのたうち回って喘[あえ]いでもがいて這い上がろうとして、それでも結局はどうにもならずに墜ちたまんまなのが良いんじゃないかッ」
lines.english: “Why does she always get saved at the last second? Isn’t it better when a girl who’s missing a few marbles and a few years gets tormented, writhes around, gasps for breath, struggles, tries to crawl her way up—only to end up falling anyway because she just can’t make it?”

lines.japanese:
「だから───僕は誓った。
　誰に誓った？　自分に誓った。
　彼女達を手に入れてやると、自分に誓った」
lines.english: “That’s why—I swore. Who’d I swear to? Myself. I swore to myself I’d get my hands on those girls.”

lines.japanese:
それは少年の日の、切なる想いであったろう。願いの言葉と、その胸の裡に燃える魂に捧げた誓いであったろう。ある夜に母親は息子に訊ねたものだ。我が腹を痛め、まさに身を二つに裂いて生み落とした分身ながらも、けして根本では理解の及ばぬ、男の子という生き物に、母親は問うたのだ。
　
　───どうして男の子って、窓を広く開けたがるんだろうね──
　
　男の子は、この物静かで控え目で、けれど靱い芯を通わせた母に答えた、そう答えるしかなかったから。

That must have been a longing from his boyhood days. A prayer and a vow dedicated to the soul burning deep within his heart. One night, his mother asked her son. To this boy—a creature she had borne with such pain, literally tearing her body in two to bring into the world, yet one she could never truly understand at its core—she posed the question.
　
　“Why do boys always want to throw the windows wide open, I wonder?” The boy answered—because he had no choice but to answer.

lines.japanese:

　その血の熱が、魂の誓いが男の子を青年にして男にと鍛え、削り、削ぎ落として鍛造しあげた。
　血の熱は毒の沼の底に澱[よど]むガスの温度であったが。
　魂はどぶ泥を覗きこんだ方がましという色に腐りきっていたが。
lines.english: ——My blood’s too hot—— That heat, that vow, hammered the boy into a young man and then a man, tempering, whittling, refining. Though the heat of his blood matched the stagnant gas at the bottom of a poison swamp. Though his soul had rotted to a color that made you wish you’d looked into a cesspool instead.

　徹底的にダメで、そして珍品じゃないとな」

lines.japanese: 「その意味でこの白子ちゃんほどぴったりなのはいない。噂を聞いてからずっと狙ってた。以前にたまさかこの港に停泊した時に見かけた時は、感動のあまりに気絶した」

lines.japanese:
「それ以来ずっと狙ってた。
　あれこれ手を尽くしてあのボロ船をこの港に呼び寄せ、渡りをつけてそしてそしてああようやく───」

lines.japanese: がっと首とほぼ垂直に反らした顔は双眸は、この薄汚れた倉庫の天上を貫き通して遙かな天の高みを仰いでいるかのよう、伸びあがった長三和音の雄叫びに耳を塞いだのはなぜか朔屋のみ、まあ手下は雇用主への義理もあろうし、クロは生憎両手が使えない。

For some reason, only Sakuya covered his ears against the long, soaring triad-like roar—well, a henchman has a duty to his employer, and unfortunately, Kuro can’t use either of his hands.

　まあまずは屋敷に戻ってお着替えだね。
　でも君には余計な衣装はごてごてと邪魔なだけ。素敵なネックレスとガーターベルトとブレスレットとアンクレットはもう用意してあるんだ。とりあえずはそれだけ身につけてくれたまへ」

lines.english: “By the way, it’s such a masterpiece that even a wire cutter can’t cut through it, and a gas torch can’t melt it.”

lines.japanese: 男はこれだけの台詞を流暢に並べたのではなく、句読点のように「アヲッ」「アヲッ」と、奇声を挟みながらで。片手を後頭部に当て、片手はズボンに股間に被せて前後に腰をひこひこと振りたくる様、目も当てられないながらも、下半身と裏腹に上半身は芯でも通したように完全に静止していたのはある種美事と言って、いいのやらどうなのやら。

One hand braced the back of his head, the other pressed over his crotch, and his hips bucked in jerky thrusts—a sight too gruesome to watch. lines.japanese: 「……そうとも言う。言葉の意味を正しく解釈したのは意外な慧眼、敬意を表するが、やはり庶民は言葉を選ぶという事を知らないのが駄目だな、この俗物が」

For the moment, he craved nothing more than a full mug—one filled to the brim with vodka, chilled until it creaked. Only something that strong could wash away this nausea. As Sakuya rubbed his temples to ease the tension, the lecture continued to pour down on him……

　それ以外の生臭物は禁止だから。体が濁る。
　毎日桃や果実を食べさせて、体から良い匂いがしてきたら、頃合いだ」
lines.english: “Kuro, in my estate, the finest, sweetest peaches will be your staple. No other foul-smelling food—it clouds the body. Feed him peaches and other fruits every day; when a pleasant scent rises from his skin, that’s the moment.”

　そのちっちゃいあそこに直接口を着けてね。
　どんなに美味なのか、思うだけで今から涎が。あっと失礼」

After all, this was “Momo Nyon-nyon”—a secret elixir known in the ancient times of the continent to promote longevity and enhance virility, though accessible only to a select few of the wealthy. Even the young girls trained as “Nyon-nyon” had short lifespans; it is said that most of them died in agony from diabetes.

If you get two or three shots, you’ll go and never come back, ending up just moaning ‘Aah, aah…’—but since Kuro-kun’s brain is already a bit of a mess, it probably won’t make much difference.”

lines.english: “On top of that, the volume of his ejaculate is outrageous, and in the end, it turns into a glue-like substance that seals off the vagina, so her belly swells up—just like a frog’s. This is the real black-and-white show.”

lines.japanese: でもちゃんと掻[か]き出してあげようと、男はそれはそれは朗らかな澄みきった笑みで、クロの前に両手の人差し指と中指添えて突きだし鉤にして、がしゅがしゅと前後させた。それは朗らかで澄みきった笑みなのに、素人娘を強引過酷に手淫して、潮を絞り出そうとする竿師の手業よりまだ兇悪な手さばきなのが恐ろしい、クロにしてみればおよそ未経験の刺激というか拷問であろうに、男の笑みだけで喉のあたりに迫り上がってきた波がある。
lines.english: But determined to make sure he got it all out, the man—with a truly cheerful, crystal-clear smile—held out his index and middle fingers of both hands in front of Kuro, forming a hook, and moved them back and forth with a “gashu, gashu” sound. It was a cheerful, crystal-clear smile, yet what was terrifying was that his movements were even more vicious than the techniques of a pimp trying to forcefully and brutally masturbate an inexperienced girl to make her squirt. For Kuro, it must have been a stimulation—or rather, torture—she’d never experienced before, yet just the man’s smile alone caused a wave to rise up in the back of her throat.

lines.japanese:
「……？　なんかよく判らないけど、
　クロ……気持ち、悪くなって……」
lines.english: “…? I don’t get it, but Kuro… I’m starting to feel sick…”

lines.japanese:
「また、ゲロしちゃうよう……、
　うえ、うぇぇ……あゥんっ」
lines.english: “Gonna puke again… Ugh, ugh… Aaah!”

lines.japanese:
しかし先ほど吐くだけ吐いて胃の腑の中味は関東軍の強奪に遭った山村の蔵のように空の空、出るのは空えづきと僅かな胃液ばかりの、嘔吐という衝撃緩和も許されずクロの精神は脆くも振り切れた。いや、ここまでよく保ったと言うべきか。いささかの妄想癖ある朔屋にしてから男の計画のあまりの酷さに気持ち悪くなり、ここは巣鴨の癲狂院、さもなくば九州帝大の精神病開放治療場なのだと思いこもうと必死でクロの事まで気が廻らない。こんな狂人が堂々と野に放たれているなど御免蒙る、だからこの倉庫は癲狂院なのだと自分に呪文をかけたが、そのキ印と格子戸もなくまともに向き合っているという状況に思い至り一層気分を悪くして膝が定まらなくなった。
　両脚がくがくさせながら、それでも立ち向かわないとこの箍の外れた現実と。彼にしては果敢に糾弾し───

lines.english:
But he’d already vomited everything; his stomach was as empty as a mountain village storehouse looted by the Kwantung Army, and all that came up was a dry retch and a trickle of acid. Denied even the shock-absorbing relief of vomiting, his fragile mind snapped. Or maybe it’s impressive he held on this long. Even Sakuya, with his head full of wild notions, felt his guts turn at the man’s scheme; he was so busy convincing himself this had to be Sugamo Asylum (tenkyōin) or the Kyushu Imperial University open-air loony bin that he couldn’t spare a thought for Kuro. “I refuse to accept that such a madman is being openly set loose in the wild,” he chanted to himself, “which is why this warehouse must be the Tenkyōin.” But when he realized he was facing this lunatic head-on—without even a sign or barred doors—he felt even more sickened, and his knees began to tremble.
　His knees were knocking, but he had to face this reality that had spun out of control. With a boldness unusual for him, he denounced—

lines.japanese: 「少女趣味というよりあんたのそれは、ソフトネクロフィリアだこの変態ッ。金持ちの高邁な趣味というたかてひどすぎる」
lines.english: “It’s not just a girly hobby—you’re a soft necrophile, pervert. Saying it’s some ‘noble rich-guy pastime’ is a stretch, man.”

lines.japanese:
「なんだっていいけどね。貧乏人に理解できるとは思わないし。
　大体この取引は、お前の船の方から持ちかけてきたんだよ？」
lines.english: “Whatever. I don’t expect you to get it, though. Besides, wasn’t it your ship that came begging for this deal?”

lines.japanese: ───今の言葉が、天が時折正直者に授けるという、宗教的な幻聴の類ではないかと疑って朔屋は、右を見て、左を見て、後ろを見て、前を見てから朔屋は最後に天を仰いで、仰いで、蜘蛛の巣のかかった天井しか見えず、天啓の徴ももらえず、しょうことなしに今一度男に問い返すしかなくて。
lines.japaneseRuby: ───今の言葉が、天が時折正直者に授けるという、宗教的な幻聴の類ではないかと疑って朔屋は、右を見て、左を見て、後ろを見て、前を見てから朔屋は最後に天を仰いで、仰いで、蜘蛛の巣のかかった天井しか見えず、天啓の[R徴^しるし]ももらえず、しょうことなしに今一度男に問い返すしかなくて。
lines.english: —He wondered if the words were a religious hallucination, the kind heaven sometimes hands honest fools. Sakuya looked right, left, behind, then ahead. Finally he looked up at the sky, and looked up again, but all he saw was a cobweb-covered ceiling. No sign from above. So he had no choice but to ask the man one more time.

lines.japanese: 「今、なんと？」
lines.english: “What’d you just say?”

lines.japanese: 「だからこの取引はそちらからの申し出、だと。いや実のところ、手間が省けて助かった」
lines.english: “So this deal was your idea, huh? Honestly, it saves me a ton of trouble.”

lines.japanese: どうやってクロを誘い出して捕らえたものか算段していると、なんと信天翁号の方からクロを払い下げる話が寄越されたらしい。金持ちの話を聞きつけた信天翁号の誰か（どうやら水夫長と航海士と見えた）が持ちかけた話のようなのだが。つまり今回クロは、朔屋のお供などではなく、右から左に遣り取りされる商品だったと、それが事の顛末だったようだ───
lines.english: Just as he was pondering how to lure Kuro out and seize him, word reached him that the Albatross itself was offering to sell Kuro off. Somebody on that ship—probably the boatswain and the navigator, drawn by the scent of easy money—had made the proposal. In other words, this time Kuro wasn’t Sakuya’s lackey at all; he was just a commodity being passed from hand to hand. That, it seemed, was the whole sorry tale—

lines.japanese:
「しかしある意味徹底していて感心するよ。
　信天翁号は仲間ですら平気で商品にする。
　───下衆どもが」
lines.japaneseRuby:
「しかしある意味徹底していて感心するよ。
　信天翁号は仲間ですら平気で商品にする。
　───[R下衆^ゲス]どもが」
lines.english: “But you have to hand it to them, they’re thorough. The Albatross treats its own crew like cargo. —Scumbags.”

lines.japanese:
二足歩行する蛙に今どき臍なんぞを見せびらかす劣等種族と罵られたところで、この男に下衆扱いされるむかっ腹には及ぶべくもないが、この場合だけはまこと正論としか言い様もないのが悔しい切ない情けない、情けなさのあまりに朔屋は顔面の神経弛緩させ、膝から崩れそうとなるところを、手を翳[かざ]して引き留めたのはなんと白スーツの脇の手下の一人の、なんとも心強い。
　……なにが心強い、こういうのは容赦なしというのだと、翳した手に握られた、黒くて硬くて底光りする鉄塊に、警鐘を乱打する警戒本能は、主と同じくぼんくらそのもの、硬い、冷たい、そして致命的な銃口を額に胸に擬されてから危機を告げたところでなんになる、もっと前に逃げろと告げるべき。
lines.english:
Even if he were cursed as an inferior race for flaunting his navel to a bipedal frog in this day and age, he couldn’t possibly match the level of contempt—being treated as a lowlife—that this man was subjected to. Yet, in this one instance, there was no other way to describe it but as the absolute truth. It was frustrating, heartbreaking, and pitiful—so pitiful that Sakuya’s face went numb with the sheer shame. —it doesn’t even come close to the rage I feel—but in this one instance, I have to admit it’s the absolute truth. Frustrating, heartbreaking, pathetic. Overwhelmed by his own patheticness, Sakuya’s facial muscles went limp, and just as he was about to collapse to his knees, he held out his hand to steady himself—and to his surprise, it was one of the henchmen standing beside the man in the white suit who caught him. How reassuring.
　What the hell’s reassuring about that? This is exactly the kind of situation where there’s no mercy. The black, hard, gleaming chunk of metal clenched in the raised hand set off alarm bells in his instincts—but like his master, those instincts were utterly dim-witted. What good would it do to warn of danger only after the hard, cold, and deadly muzzle was pressed against his forehead or chest? He should have told him to run away much sooner.

lines.japanese:
「さて商品を目出度く受領したところで、
　代価の支払いというのが、
　正当な段取だ───」
lines.english: “Now that we’ve successfully received the goods, payment for them is the proper next step—”

lines.japanese: 代価の支払いというて拳銃突きつける奴があるかと罵るより先に、朔屋は男が代金を納めたスーツケースの類持ち合わせず、それどころか財布の一つも取り出そうとする気配ないのに、首筋に冷気を感じた。知らずに流した汗、悪く冷たい、この手の汗を感じてろくな目に遭った例しがない。
lines.english: Before he could even curse, “Who points a gun just to collect payment?”—he felt a chill on the back of his neck. The man wasn’t carrying any suitcase or the like to hold the payment, and in fact showed no sign of even reaching for a wallet. It was the sweat he’d broken out in—a nasty, cold sweat. He’d never had a good experience whenever he felt this kind of sweat.

lines.japanese: 金持ちは、朔屋にクロの代価を引き渡す事は忘れなかった。───いや。渡そうとして、いかにも直前で気を変えた風に、
lines.english: The rich man didn’t forget to hand Sakuya the payment for Kuro. —No. He tried to hand it over, but just as he was about to, he acted as if he’d changed his mind at the very last moment,

lines.japanese: 「しかし今のご時世、いろいろとお上の目が厳しくてね。人身売買などがばれたら、たちまち破滅だ」
lines.english: “But these days, the authorities are watching closely. If human trafficking or anything like that got out, it’d be instant ruin.”

lines.japanese: 「だからこの子を『身請け』した、なんて事自体なかったことにさせてもらう」
lines.english: “So let’s just pretend this whole business of ‘buying this child’s freedom’ never happened.”

lines.japanese:
「幸いそっちからの立ち合いは、
　君一人のようだし」
lines.english: “Fortunately, it seems you’re the only one here from your side.”

lines.japanese:
それ以上は言わずとも知れる。信天翁号のような最低の船に無理矢理徴募された者が陸に使いに出され、大人しく戻ると期待するのは己の右足につまずいてすっ転ぶような間抜けくらいだろう。朔屋自身この上陸に逃亡を思った事は一度や二度ではない。
　だから。
　今更新米船員の一人や二人が戻らなかったところで、気にする船の古株達などいないという事。
lines.english: No need to say more. Expecting someone pressed onto a wretched tub like the Albatross to be sent ashore on an errand and return meekly is as foolish as tripping over your own right foot and falling flat on your face. Sakuya himself had thought of using this shore leave to escape more than once or twice. That’s why. Even if one or two of the newest crew members didn’t return now, none of the ship’s veterans would bat an eye.

lines.japanese:
「いやいやいや、待って、考え直そうよ？
　そらあの連中は俺が一人二人いなくなったって、気にもしないだろうが」
lines.english: “No, no, no, wait—let’s think this through, okay? Sure, those guys probably wouldn’t even notice if one or two of us disappeared.”

lines.japanese: そうやって自分の無価値を自分で告げるうちに、朔屋は少しだけ泣きたくなったが、どうにかこらえて話を引き延ばす、引き延ばしたところで事態が好転するとも思えなかったけれど。
lines.english: Declaring his own worthlessness, Sakuya felt a faint urge to cry, but he held it in and dragged out the talk—even though he didn’t think it would do any good.

lines.japanese: 「銭金の事にかけちゃ悪魔の猟犬よりしつこいぞあいつら。金が払われなかったら、きっと取り立てに来る───」
lines.english: “When it comes to money, those guys are more persistent than the devil’s hounds. If they don’t get paid, they’ll definitely come after us to collect—”

lines.japanese:
「あの船で不当に働かされている女児を保護した。
　それでなんとも簡単に片づきそうな気がするが。
　あんな腐れた船の言い分と、この港にそれなりに金を落としている僕とでは、さてどちらが有利かねえ」
lines.english: “I rescued the girl they were exploiting on that ship. Should be an easy wrap-up, right? A rotten tub of a ship versus a customer who spends real money in this port—which side do you think wins?”

lines.japanese: 「……ごもっとも」
lines.english: “……You’re absolutely right.”

lines.japanese: 「それに、あんな海の破落戸ども、港に停泊するだけでどれだけの怨みと反感を買っているのやら。お前達、自分達がどれだけ忌み嫌われているか、もう少し自覚したらどうだ？」
lines.japaneseRuby: 「それに、あんな海の[R破落戸^ごろつき]ども、港に停泊するだけでどれだけの怨みと反感を買っているのやら。お前達、自分達がどれだけ忌み嫌われているか、もう少し自覚したらどうだ？」
lines.english: “Besides, just by dropping anchor in the harbor, those sea ruffians must be stirring up a whole lot of resentment and hostility. Why don’t you guys try to be a little more aware of just how much you’re despised?”

lines.japanese:
そんなのは今更言われずとも痛感している朔屋であり、あの不運の一夜を契機に船に連れこまれていなかったら、彼だって信天翁号に石を投げる側に位置していたのだ。
　正論は美しくそして時に残酷であるという。うっかり素直に頷[うなず]いてしまったはいいものの、ついに朔屋の全身各部位は、意識の統御を離れて出鱈目てんで勝手に活動開始した。左脚は伏せて射線を回避しようとし、口は泣き叫んで慈悲を乞う準備、腹は恐怖に膀胱を締めあげ、手は無意味に目を塞ごうとする、まとまりに欠けることこの上ない。その中で朔屋の心は───
lines.japaneseRuby:
そんなのは今更言われずとも痛感している朔屋であり、あの不運の一夜を[R契機^きっかけ]に船に連れこまれていなかったら、彼だって信天翁号に石を投げる側に位置していたのだ。
　正論は美しくそして時に残酷であるという。うっかり素直に頷[うなず]いてしまったはいいものの、ついに朔屋の全身各部位は、意識の統御を離れて出鱈目てんで勝手に活動開始した。左脚は伏せて射線を回避しようとし、口は泣き叫んで慈悲を乞う準備、腹は恐怖に膀胱を締めあげ、手は無意味に目を塞ごうとする、まとまりに欠けることこの上ない。その中で朔屋の心は───
lines.english:
Sakuya knew it already, without anyone saying so; had he not been lured aboard that fateful night, he, too, would have been among those throwing stones at the Albatross.
　Sound reasoning is beautiful—and sometimes cruel. He had nodded, carelessly, but now every part of his body broke free and started moving on its own. His left leg dived for cover, his mouth opened to wail and beg, his stomach clenched his bladder in fear, and his hands flailed to shield his eyes—a scene of total disarray. And in the middle of it all, Sakuya’s mind—

lines.japanese: <01>どうにかクロを助け出そうと願った
lines.english: 01>He prayed that he could somehow rescue Kuro

lines.japanese: <01>何をしても無駄と諦めた
lines.english: 01>He gave up, realizing that nothing he did would make a difference.

lines.japanese:
好き勝手に自己主張する体のあちこちの中、右脚だけは辛うじて地に着いていたのは、どうにか土性骨残していた為でなく、主と同じくすくたれ者であるあまりに、泰然と腰を抜かしていたというにすぎないだろう。足が腰を抜かすとは奇怪な謂[い]いだが。ともかく、その右だけが心に沿わせられると感じた時に、朔屋は本当に、自分でも信じられない事に、一歩踏み出していたのである。かすかに呻[うめ]くクロを目指して。もしかしたらその時、朔屋のご先祖の一人が幽冥の通路を越えて合力してくれていたのかも知れない。朔屋の如き駄目男を排出した血筋でも、家系図総ざらえにすれば一人くらいは気骨備えた丈夫があったのかも。
　朔屋にしてから自分の行動が意外であったのなら、金持ちの方の驚きはいかばかりか。向かってくる彼に対して、やや鼻白んだように瞬きさえ。
lines.english:
Amid all the parts of his body asserting themselves willy-nilly, the only part that was barely touching the ground was his right leg—not because he had somehow managed to retain a shred of his earthly nature, but simply because, being just as much of a good-for-nothing as his master, it had calmly gone limp. “A leg going limp” is a strange way of putting it, but anyway, just as he felt that only that right leg was obeying his will, Sakuya—to his own disbelief—had actually taken a step forward. He lurched toward Kuro, who was letting out a faint groan. Maybe at that moment one of his ancestors had crossed over from the dead to lend a hand. Even in a bloodline that had produced a good-for-nothing like him, if you combed the whole family tree you might find at least one sturdy soul with backbone.
　If Sakuya was startled by his own move, the rich man’s shock was off the charts; he even blinked, taken aback.

lines.japanese:
「なんだなぁ。なんのつもりだ。
　銃を怖がる程度の頭もないのか？
　それともとうとうおかしくなったわけ？」
lines.english: “What’s this? What the hell do you think you’re doing? Don’t you have enough sense to be afraid of a gun? Or have you finally lost your mind?”

lines.japanese:
「や、その……すんません、
　自分でもなんか、その」
lines.english: “Uh, well… I’m sorry, I guess even I, well…”

lines.japanese: 踏み出しておきながらどこまでも強きにへりくだり式で、やはり朔屋の行動は蛮勇どころか、逃げ出す方向を間違っただけと見るべきか───
lines.english: Having taken that step forward, yet adopting an attitude of unending subservience to the strong—should we view his actions not as reckless bravery, but simply as having chosen the wrong direction to flee?───

lines.japanese: 「でもあの、品だけ渡して金持ってかなかったら、船に戻った時、俺絶対死ぬほどの折檻くらうんで」
lines.english: “But, um, if I just hand over the goods and don’t take the money, I’ll definitely get beaten to death when I get back to the ship.”

lines.japanese:
「死ぬような目……、
　今か、後か、どっちがいいのか、
　ううう、どっちも厭だぁ……」
lines.japaneseRuby:
「死ぬような目……、
　今か、後か、どっちがいいのか、
　ううう、どっちも[R厭^いや]だぁ……」
lines.english: “Those eyes like he’s about to die… Now or later—which is better? Uuuu, I hate both of them…”

lines.japanese: ぐずぐずと半泣き、鼻水まで垂らして、それでもまた一歩を踏んだところを見ると、いかな理不尽な罰であろうと、船での鉄拳制裁は眼前の銃と同じくらいの恐怖を朔屋の骨身に刻んでいると見える。迫ってくるといっても手に寸鉄さえなく、おまけにいい歳した男が泣きを入れながらでは迫力は微塵もなく、白スーツはすぐに気を取り直し、手下に唇の端吊り上げて、もう言わずもがな、さっさと始末をつけろの合図に、かちゃりと金属音が答えた。撃鉄を起こす音だった。いよいよもってもうお終い、こんなところで一巻の、否一巻にも充たない朔屋の人生に終止符が───
lines.english: Hesitant, on the verge of tears, snot even dripping from his nose—yet seeing him take another step forward, it seemed that no matter how unreasonable the punishment might be, the iron-fisted discipline on the ship had etched a terror into Sakuya’s very bones equal to that of the gun before his eyes. Even though he was advancing, he didn’t even have a gun in his hand, and on top of that, a grown man crying like that had not a shred of menace about him. The man in the white suit quickly regained his composure, raised the corner of his mouth at his henchman—a signal that needed no words, telling him to finish the job—and a metallic click answered. It was the sound of the hammer being cocked. The end. Right here, the last page—no, not even a whole page—of Sakuya’s life was being torn off—

lines.japanese:
銃口を向けられたまま暫時の緊張を強いられた時、なんで相手はまず撃たないのか訝しむのは、修羅場を踏んだ経験のあるものか余程の阿呆くらいである。中途半端にそのどちらでもない朔屋は、あっさりと銃の圧力に屈した。クロは可哀相は可哀相なれど、あの変態異常性欲者に飼われている限りは、少なくとも自分よりは長生きできるはず。そんな相手を助けようとするのは暴虎馮河の勇の愚行、朔屋が銃口からもクロからも逃れるように、手が勝手に目を覆うに任せたのは、あながち無意味とは言いきれまい。
　少なくとも自分に鉛玉がめりこむその銃光は見ずに済む……が、視覚を閉ざした事により拡大された聴覚が捉えた、かちゃりと金属音の、それ撃鉄を起こす響き、いよいよもってもうお終い、こんなところで一巻の、否一巻にも充たない朔屋の人生に終止符が───

lines.english:
When a man’s got a gun shoved in his face, only a fool or a veteran of the meat grinder wonders why the trigger hasn’t been pulled yet. Sakuya, stuck somewhere in the middle, couldn’t meet that standard. The barrel’s pressure broke him. Poor Kuro, sure, but as long as he stayed with that perverted freak, he’d probably live longer than Sakuya. Trying to rescue him would be the height of foolish bravery—like a tiger charging into a river. So when Sakuya’s hands flew up to shield his eyes from both the muzzle and Kuro, the gesture wasn’t entirely without point.
　At least I won’t have to see the flash of the gun as the lead bullet buries itself in me… but the heightened hearing brought on by blocking my vision picked up the clack of metal—the sound of the hammer being cocked. It’s finally over. Here, in a place like this, the final chapter—no, not even a full chapter—of Sakuya’s life comes to an end—

lines.japanese: がぁぁぁぁん！
lines.english: Gaaaaaah!

lines.japanese:
「ぎゃああああああ！
　撃たれたぁぁっ」
lines.english: “Aaaaaaargh! I’ve been shot!”

lines.japanese: 鳴った音は高く、朔屋はとうとう数滴パンツの中に失禁で、堤防が全決壊しなかっただけでも立派と言えて、その割りこんだ音は彼のみならず対峙していた連中にとっても意想外の事であり、全員の動きが瞬時に凝結する。
lines.english: The sharp ring of it made Sakuya finally lose control, leaking a few drops of urine into his pants. It was a feat in itself that the dam hadn’t completely burst. That sudden sound took not only him but also the men facing him by surprise, and everyone’s movements froze instantly.

lines.japanese:
そう───銃を構えた手下にとってもボスにとっても、思いも寄らない轟音だった。銃声だってここまで重いものか。実際拳銃は、銃把こそ手下の手の温度を帯びていたけれど銃身に炸裂熱無く硝煙の揺らめく筋も見えず、朔屋の体で痛むのは馬鹿声張り上げた喉くらい、どこにも焦げ穴一つ開いていない。
　では轟音はどこから、それは倉庫の外から、壁を隔てて遠いのに、その音源の凄まじさが窺えるほどに破壊力を蔵した音、遠大な。
lines.english:
That’s right—for both the henchman holding the gun and his boss, it was an unexpected, thunderous roar. Could a gunshot really be this heavy? In fact, though the pistol’s grip was warm from the henchman’s hand, the barrel showed no signs of explosive heat or flickering trails of gunpowder smoke; the only part of Sakuya’s body that ached was his throat, strained from shouting, and there wasn’t a single burn hole anywhere.
　So where the hell did that roar come from? Outside the warehouse—far off, walled off, yet still heavy enough to rattle the air.

lines.japanese: 次いで走りこんできたのが、ボスに侍っていたのと同様のダークスーツの男で、つんのめり、手を鶏の飛べない翼と泳がせて、扉を抜けて一声、
lines.english: Next to burst in was a man in a dark suit, just like the one who’d been tending to the boss. He stumbled forward, flapping his arms like a chicken’s wings that couldn’t fly, burst through the door, and let out a cry,

lines.japanese: 「だ、旦那ッ。旦那の三番倉庫で爆発が、火がッ、いきなり燃え広がってっ」
lines.english: “M-Master! Warehouse Three—it’s blown! It’s on fire! It’s spreading!”

lines.japanese: 外で見張っていたらしい手下から叩きつけられた報せで、面々の石化していた体が肉に戻るより先に、このタイミングで意識取り戻したのはクロ、澱んでいた眸[ひとみ]に光が戻った、とは言っても普段が普段だからたかが知れており、

lines.english: The news, delivered by the henchman who’d been keeping watch outside, jolted Kuro awake—before the others’ stone-still bodies had even softened back to flesh. Light flickered in his clouded eyes—though, given his usual state, it wasn’t much to write home about, and

lines.japanese:
「注射、やめてぇっ、
　豚さんとトモダチも、なんか怖いよぉ……」
lines.english: “Stop the shot, please! Even Piggy and my friends are kind of scary…”

lines.japanese:
急転した事態を全くよそに、断線前の記憶を引きずって身悶えする、がそんなのは耳から吊り下げられた兎よりも甲斐ない抵抗に過ぎず、屈強な手下にかかっては難なく手をひねられてそこまでの、そこまでになったろうとも、爆発音に虚を衝[つ]かれてさえいなかったなら。身を捩り、ひねり、髪乱す白子の娘に一瞬だけ遅れた反応がその手下にとっての命運を分けた。金持ちの部下としても、男としても。
　人間の内心を悉く見透かして恐れられた山中の怪、サトリの魔物に傷を与え追い払ったのは、猟師が折ろうとした粗朶が手の裡から弾けて、偶然に怪にぶち当たった事に因るという。狙うという、心の働きの外で起こる偶発時には天眼通とて対処は困難の故事だが、この時同様の事が生じた。

lines.english:
Completely oblivious to the sudden turn of events, he writhed in agony, clinging to the memories from before the connection was severed—but such resistance was even more futile than that of a rabbit hung by its ears. In the hands of a burly henchman, his wrist would have been twisted effortlessly, and that would have been the end of it—had he not been caught off guard by the explosion. That split-second lag in reacting to the Shirako girl—twisting, writhing, hair askew—sealed the henchman’s fate. Both as a man under a wealthy master and as a man in his own right.
　It is said that the monster of Satori—a mountain apparition feared for its ability to see right through a person’s innermost thoughts—was wounded and driven off not by any deliberate action, but simply because a thin twig the hunter had been trying to snap snapped from his hand and accidentally struck the monster. They say that when an accident lands outside intent, even the divine eye (tengentsu) has trouble handling it—and yet, something like that happened right then.

lines.japanese: クロの身悶えは、俎板に釘で頭を打ち留められた鰻と同じく痙攣的な反射であり、彼女自身意図していなかった力と角度で、六尺棒が両膝の間からすっぽ抜け、なまじ縛りつけて抑えられていたのが瞬発的に放たれただけに、反動で加速され、宙を奔った速度は目に追えないほど。クロの足から外れたと思った瞬間には───身の毛のよだつ音がした。爆発音や銃声とも異質で、くぐもって、なのに男にとっては聞くだけでも身の毛がよだつ。

lines.english: Kuro's writhing was a convulsive reflex, like an eel with its head nailed to a chopping board. With a force and angle she had never intended, the six-foot pole slipped from between her knees. Precisely because she had been tied and held in check, its sudden release accelerated it with the recoil. It shot through the air faster than the eye could follow. The instant it came free of her legs—a hair-raising sound. Unlike a blast or a gunshot. Muffled, yet enough to make any man's hair stand merely to hear it.

lines.japanese:
六尺棒は。
　朔屋に銃を向けていた手下の。
　その股間に。
　残酷なまでに深々と。
lines.english:
The six-foot pole.
The henchman aiming a gun at Sakuya.
His groin.
Cruelly deep—

lines.japanese:
ああ───
　めりこんで。
lines.english:
Ah—
It struck home.

lines.japanese:
たまらない間の中で、ぶくぶくと小泡が弾ける。
　かちかちがちがちと硬く細かい音伴って。
lines.english:
In an unbearable interval, tiny bubbles broke and foamed.
Accompanied by a hard, fine clacking and chattering.

lines.japanese: 「あ……え……ごめん、なさい……？」
lines.english: “Ah… Eh… I'm sorry…?”

lines.japanese:
手下が、がちがちと歯を鳴らしながら悶絶していた。
　南方熊楠翁によれば、金的に深刻なる痛打を受けたる場合、股間の痛みもさりながら、余りの衝撃に神経回路の齟齬が発生し、歯の根が合わなくなるという。この記述が正しいことを確認した朔屋は、同性として身の裡が縮み上がる思いだったけれど、かといって手下に全く同情はできなかった。自分に銃を突きつけてくる相手にそこまで寛大になれるほど、朔屋は人間ができていない。

The henchman writhed in agony, his teeth chattering.

Having confirmed this account, Sakuya felt himself shrink inside as a fellow man. But he could muster no sympathy for the henchman. He had not developed enough generosity to extend it to someone pointing a gun at him.

lines.japanese: 耐久力を余程信頼していたのか、どずんと床に伏した手下に金持ち見る間に色を失ったし、外から駆けこんできた手下の報告もまた衝撃だったようで、金持ち殿、クロと戸口の外を代わる代わりに睨[にら]んで葛藤の内心ありありと、選んだのは外に駆け出すあたり、爆発したのは余程重要なものの倉庫だったよう。
lines.english: Perhaps the rich man had placed considerable faith in his subordinate's endurance. As the fellow dropped heavily to the floor, he visibly paled. The report from the henchman who had rushed in was apparently another shock. The wealthy gentleman glared alternately at Kuro and the doorway, his inner conflict plain. He chose to run outside. Whatever had exploded must have been an important warehouse.

lines.japanese: 「あ、旦那、こいつ等はどうするんでっ？」
lines.english: “Ah, sir, what about these two?”

lines.japanese:
「バカ、いいから、どうせ逃げられない、
　今はそれより向こうを！
　なんて事だ、
　あそこには今度の商談用の……っ」
lines.english: “Idiot! Never mind. They can't escape anyway. The other place comes first! What a disaster. In there, for the coming deal, I've got—”

lines.japanese: 金持ちとしては手下に場を任せたつもりだったのかも知れないが、手下にしてみれば常にボスの傍にあるのが第一優先事項であったようで、朔屋とクロを憎さげに睨[にら]みつけてから、結局選んだのが外に飛びだしていったボスを追う事であったたという。自らの判断能力を放棄するような手下しか抱えていないあたり、このボスの底、やはり浅いのだろう。
lines.english: Perhaps the rich man meant to leave his subordinates in charge here. For them, however, staying beside their boss evidently took priority. After glaring hatefully at Sakuya and Kuro, the man ultimately chose to follow his employer outside. A boss whose men had surrendered their own judgment must, after all, have been a shallow one.

lines.japanese:
「てめえら、どうせ逃げられねえからな、
　大人しくしてろや……っ」
lines.english: “You bastards can't escape anyway. Stay put…!”

lines.japanese: 捨て台詞までがボスの模倣で、報せに来たのもまた返す刀で走り出して、倉庫には朔屋とクロの二人だけ（意識不明の手下は数に入らぬとして）、いよいよ空しい広さが広がるばかり。朔屋はクロとしばし呆然と目を交わして、そして彼女を担ぎ上げて扉に駆けた。まだクロの手には縛りつけられたまま六尺棒が残っているが、解いている余裕はないし、外に見張りがあろうとも荏苒手をこまねいているだけに留まるほど、朔屋といえど脳味噌に鬆は入っていない。よし、たとい外に出た瞬間に敢え無く捕まる可能性もあるが、一筋の蜘蛛の糸はあるはず、ここに残っていてはやがて戻ってきた誰かに確実に捕まる。それだけの判断力は残していて、とにかく、悶絶した護衛には目もくれず、ここを先途と逃げ出す朔屋の、一応自分を助けてくれた事になるクロを肩に担ぎあげると、か細い声で囁かれた。

lines.english: Even his parting threat imitated his boss. The messenger, too, turned and ran out. Only Sakuya and Kuro remained in the warehouse—not counting the unconscious henchman—and its empty breadth expanded still further. They exchanged a stunned look for a while. Then Sakuya hoisted her and ran for the door. The six-foot pole was still tied to her hands, but there was no time to undo it. Even he was not so hollow-brained as to sit helplessly, regardless of any guards outside. Yes, they might be caught the instant they emerged. But there must be a spider's thread of hope. Remain here, and someone would eventually return and certainly catch them. He retained that much judgment. Without another look at the unconscious guard, he fled while he could. As he shouldered Kuro, who had, in a sense, saved him, she whispered weakly—

lines.japanese:
「……あんね、クロさっき、棒、振り回す？
　ぶんぶんして、あの人のお股に当たっちゃった時」
lines.english: “…You know, just now, when Kuro was swinging the pole? Going whoosh-whoosh, and it hit that man's crotch…”

lines.japanese: 「いい、それ以上言うな」
lines.english: “Enough. Don't say any more.”

lines.japanese:
「でもぉ……なんか……。
　くちゃっ
　って、そんな感じ、で、手にまだ……。
　くちゃっ　　　　───って」
lines.english:
“But… Something… Squish. It felt like that. Still in my hands…
Squish—”

lines.japanese: 「言うな、だから言うなぁぁぁっ」
lines.english: “Don't say it! I said don't say it!”

lines.japanese: その感触がなにを物語っていたのか、想像するだけでおぞましく、ちょっと内股になりながら、倉庫を転び出る───
lines.japaneseRuby: その感触がなにを物語っていたのか、想像するだけでおぞましく、ちょっと内股になりながら、倉庫を[R転^まろ]び出る───
lines.english: The mere thought of what that sensation meant was horrifying. Knees a little turned inward, he stumbled out of the warehouse—

lines.japanese: 「あと、それから……」
lines.english: “And, also…”

lines.japanese: 「後にしてくれ、今はそれどころじゃない」
lines.english: “Later. This isn't the time.”

lines.japanese: 「あい……でも、あんがと」
lines.english: “Okay… But, thank you.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese:
「朔屋さん、クロのこと、助けようってしてくれた。
　なんとなくわかったの……。
　だから、あんがと」
lines.english: “Mr. Sakuya, you tried to help Kuro. I could sort of tell… So, thank you.”

Yet for some reason his ears grew hot, like those of an innocent adolescent boy. He himself did not understand why, and was disconcerted.
